reason: Formal-verification proof search, not resource management; seL4/Isabelle corpus is huge and slow, and the repo is unconfirmed as the official artifact.
Tier-aware LSM compaction is core storage systems with a GitHub+Zenodo artifact; only the QLC/SLC tier split must be emulated on our NVMe.
Offline Python trace-analysis tool runs trivially here with released traces, but it is observability modeling rather than resource management and the extension space is modest.
Learned-DBMS robustness study with no repo located; hard requirement of an official implementation is unmet.
Range filters inside a KV store are classic user-space storage work that fits the machine as-is, with an obvious policy/tuning design space.
Mask-aware caching and scheduling for single-GPU diffusion serving fits 24 GB; caching policy and admission heuristics are naturally swappable.
Data-preprocessing pipeline with a learned parser selector is systems-adjacent; HPC-scale evaluation needs a much reduced document set locally.
CPU-only lossless compression runs anywhere, but the located repo may hold only datasets and the contribution is a fairly closed codec.
IaC static bug-finding is outside OS resource management, and the headline metric (detection quality) cannot be validated without real cloud providers.
CPU-GPU task orchestration for GNN training is a plausible single-node target, but the thin note leaves artifact completeness and scale unknown.
Explicitly targets one memory-constrained GPU with Triton kernels; compression-policy knobs give clear hypotheses, though it leans ML-training rather than OS.
LLM-bootstrapped DBMS knob tuning with no repo located and an external LLM endpoint dependency.
Approximation-versus-latency serving system is systems-adjacent and single-node, but the note gives no evidence of artifact completeness.
Learned query-optimizer work is far from OS resource management and no artifact was located.
Fault-injection bug finding on distributed JVM systems; reliability testing rather than resource management, and targets are inherently multi-node.
Self-contained user-space C++ index with a Zenodo artifact that needs no privileged features; structure/heuristic swaps are easy hypotheses.
Selective recompute is a genuine memory-vs-compute policy, but sequence parallelism needs tensor parallelism and Megatron-LM is a huge fast-moving upstream repo.
Cardinality estimation is DB modeling rather than OS, and no artifact was found.
Huge public FaaS traces enable trace-driven cold-start/scheduling simulation on this machine, though the team must supply the simulator since the artifact is data plus notebooks.
CPU-only LLM-serving workload generator with released traces is trivially runnable, but improving a generator's fidelity is a narrower hypothesis than improving a serving mechanism.
Full AE badges and GA102 does support 2:4 sparse tensor cores, but this is kernel/sparsity co-design rather than resource management, and MoE checkpoints must be shrunk for 24 GB.
Elastic provisioning policy needs a cloud account for its evaluation and no artifact was located; only a home-built simulation would remain.
GPU/DRAM/SSD KV-cache tiering is an ideal topic, but no repo was located so the system would have to be reimplemented from the paper.
Open testbed with 17 index advisors is a solid reproduction base, but physical database index selection sits well outside OS resource management.
CPU-only compression scheme but no artifact was found, and the multiresolution encoding result is fairly closed.
Memory-layout work is relevant and single-node runs are meaningful, but the only link is an anonymous.4open.science repo and headline results are supercomputer-scale.
Predictor-free sparsity with simulated memory hierarchies runs on one GPU at 7-8B scale; the masking/cache policy is a clean swap point.
Award-winning user-space C++ succinct data store fits 125 GiB RAM with no privileged features and root-free baselines.
LSM level-capacity/run-count design space on RocksDB is textbook storage systems, single-node NVMe, with a large well-defined space of policy variants to test.
GPU model swapping between host RAM and one GPU is exactly this machine's profile; only the multi-GPU scheduling half and CUDA-version-sensitive API redirection are risks.
The released tuner library is pure user space, but every evaluated target needs Kubernetes, Azure, or containers, so a substitute tunable system must be found.
Adaptive row/column layout selection is a real storage policy, but it requires a full TiDB+TiFlash deployment which is very heavy for 10 weeks on one host.
Pipelined CPU-GPU sharding under a VRAM budget on llama.cpp with an MLSys AE repo plus Zenodo archive; the A5000 + 125 GiB host RAM is the exact target regime.
Adaptive JIT query execution is a runtime contribution that fits one node, but the research-grade LLVM-heavy build is real friction.
Single-Ampere-GPU compression kernels run here, but it is a format/kernel contribution with limited resource-management angle and unknown artifact completeness.
Only the planner and runtime simulator half is reproducible on one CPU machine, but simulator accuracy and search-space improvements are genuinely testable hypotheses.
Dynamic-shape ML compiler is systems-adjacent and single-GPU sufficient, but the build is large with CUDA/TF/PyTorch pinning risk against driver 535.
Out-of-core GNN training explicitly designed for limited GPU memory matches the machine, though artifact completeness and dataset size are unverified.
A learned performance predictor validated across four accelerators we do not have, released as what looks like an anonymized microkernel-only artifact.
Flash-cache admission and prefetching evaluated entirely offline on released Meta traces; policy, residency model, and objective function are all swappable — an anchor-grade fit.
Latch-free in-memory B+-tree scales down to 32 threads with the contention story intact, but the shared IndexResearch repo's completeness is unknown.
User-space C++ framework for making static indexes updatable runs anywhere and has an obvious space of reconstruction/amortization policy variants.
Single-machine parallel batch processing scales from 48 to 16 cores naturally, but the decentralized-exchange domain is far from OS topics and the C++ dependency tree is heavy.
The artifact ships a trace-driven cluster-scheduling simulator, exactly the allowed case; only the physical-cluster half is out of reach, capping claims at simulated goodput.
Unified paged memory pool plus adapter prefetch on a single GPU is a memory-management problem with many admission/eviction policy hypotheses; only TP experiments must be dropped.
Input-pipeline optimizer defaults to local execution with distributed workers optional; the optimizer's decision policies are a clear extension surface.
Trace-replayable disk placement policy with good topic fit, but no official repo was found so everything would need reimplementation.
Model fetch and loading cold-start work is measurable on one GPU plus local NVMe, but the placement and network-contention design needs several GPUs and servers.
Single-GPU temporal-graph framework with no official repo found; graph-algorithm execution is also far from OS resource management.
Activation offloading is a good memory-management topic, but the design is built around a multi-GPU node and ultra-long context, needing a severe and possibly unfaithful scale-down.
Lookahead prefetch of IVF clusters from CPU to GPU under tight memory budgets is a prefetching-policy problem that runs single-GPU; only the multi-GPU scheduler is lost.
FP6 kernels on FP16 tensor cores match sm_86 and CUDA 11.8 exactly, but it is a quantization-kernel contribution and experiments must drop from 70B to 7-13B.
Core lookup structure is a self-contained C++ library, but the headline evaluation is a multi-node cloud deployment and the repo has no CI and was last pushed in 2021.
CPU-only stream compiler with a Zenodo AE artifact runs cleanly here, though query compilation is systems-adjacent rather than core OS.
Fully user-space rsync/dsync extension with client and server on one host; only the WAN numbers are lost since tc/netem needs root.
The plan-search compiler and cost model are user-space and studyable on one GPU, but end-to-end speedup claims require multiple GPUs, limiting validation to the cost model.
Federated-learning client sampling is mostly an algorithmic contribution; FedScale simulation fits one GPU but rounds must be scaled down substantially.
CPU offloading on a single 24 GB consumer GPU is precisely this machine, though 3D Gaussian Splatting is a narrow application domain and artifact completeness is unstated.
Released vLLM fork plus simulator make this a clean reproduce-or-improve target; re-testing the speculative-decoding claims at 24 GB scale is itself a strong hypothesis.
GPU/CPU wave-buffer KV-cache storage engine is exactly the memory-constrained profile, but the 80 GB GPU baseline forces meaningful context scale-down.
Profile-guided optimization is user-space compiler work, but fresh profile collection needs perf/LBR which is blocked, so the project is confined to shipped profiles.
CPU-only and easy to run, but learned spatial-index packing is a DB-internals topic with limited OS resource-management content.
DRAM-only C++ hybrid index runs here, but the best numbers use a 4-socket server versus our single socket and 16 cores.
Idle-memory harvesting is an ideal OS memory topic, but the coordinator relies on a kernel module that cannot be loaded without root, gutting the cross-application story.
The caching angle is relevant and CPU-only, but no artifact was found and HE library builds add friction for a narrow result.
Single-GPU spatial sharing is an unusually good topic match, but CUPTI/Nsight profiling needs root and the artifact assumes Docker on a V100, leaving only the released CSVs and MPS path.
Prefill scheduling and preemption with a Zenodo artifact and public workloads, but the prefill-decode disaggregated assumption forces two small co-located instances on one GPU.
Textbook CPU-only cache-replacement policy work with an obvious improvement space, but the scout confirmed no public repository could be located.
The SLO-aware batching and rolling KV cache run on one GPU, but the headline FPS-scaling claim depends on multi-GPU pipelining that cannot be reproduced.
Clean single-GPU user-space artifact that runs as-is, but a parallel parser is data-processing rather than an OS resource-management problem.
Single-node multi-version storage engine with an open repo, though the temporal-graph domain narrows relevance and artifact completeness is unstated.
Pure user-space cache eviction/promotion library with a trace-driven harness; only absolute numbers suffer since the README expects 32+ physical cores per socket.
CPU-only concurrent learned index that fits 32 threads well, but learned-index structure work is DB-internals-leaning with a bounded extension space.
GPU isolation and memory management built purely on CUDA streams needs no root and fits one A5000; the main risk is the serverless runtime and CUDA/driver 535 compatibility.
User-space live patching is interesting but no repo was located and the Redis Cluster target adds multi-process setup for a narrow result.
Tensor caching, prefetch and migration across GPU/DRAM/NVMe is exactly this machine's tiering profile; only model sizes need scaling down.
Single-GPU GNN kernel transformations with no official repo found, and the topic is compiler/algebraic rather than resource management.
CPU-only DNN serving inside a lightweight DBMS scales down naturally, but the note gives no evidence of a complete artifact and the design is fairly specialized.
Single-node RocksDB-backed storage engine builds in user space with single-machine benchmarks, but the compliance headline means an improvement must retarget the storage/query path.
Code and latency datasets are released and models train on one GPU, but latency prediction for NAS is ML-for-hardware rather than OS, and the 85 edge platforms are unavailable.
